minutes.headline: ZBA found no concerns with a two-story addition and apartment at 36 Summer Street, then sent a driveway permit back to the building inspector
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals reviewed a development plan for a two-story addition to an automotive building at 36 Summer Street, with garage bays below and an apartment above. The addition was moved from the east to the west side, so it meets setbacks and avoids the floodplain. The board moved that it had no concerns, then moved to refer a Land Court-remanded driveway permit matter for 233 Lancaster Avenue to the building inspector.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals reviewed a plan for a two-story addition with garage bays and an apartment at 36 Summer Street and moved that it had no concerns.
The review was approved on the condition that the applicant comply with all licenses, regulations and requirements of other boards with jurisdiction.
The board moved to send a driveway permit application for 233 Lancaster Avenue back to the building inspector, as the Land Court remand directs.
A letter noting the board's vote is to go with the referral to the building inspector.
The addition was moved from the east to the west side of the lot, so it meets setbacks and stays out of the floodplain.

why_it_matters: The 36 Summer Street addition can go ahead to other boards' permits, and it adds a dwelling unit to an automotive property.
The driveway permit at 233 Lancaster Avenue now returns to the building inspector, so the next decision on it will come from that office rather than this board.
